unit: Approval Gate delivery-key derivation (send_key / dry_key / communication_id)
description: Every SND- delivery key on the Communications tab is in the widened 16-hex-character format; any surviving 8-character key is a pre-F-02 legacy row that the current code can no longer match.
why_it_exists: F-02 widened the delivery key from 32 to 64 bits. The change is deliberately not backward compatible: a Communications row written under the old 8-character key will not be matched by the new 16-character key, so the first write per approval after the change appends a second row instead of updating the first. The census counts rows by key format to size that one-time effect and to find any approval still stranded on a legacy key.

old_8_char.produced_by: WF4 'Approval Gate' code node BEFORE finding F-02. A single 32-bit FNV-1a pass over deliveryIdentity with offset basis 0x811c9dc5, rendered as ('0000000' + h.toString(16)).slice(-8) = 8 lowercase hex characters.
old_8_char.why_replaced: 32 bits reaches roughly a 1% birthday-collision probability by about 10,000 deliveries. A collision means two different approved deliveries share communication_id and send_key, so one silently overwrites the other's Communications row and the sheet can no longer answer whether a particular legal communication was sent.

new_16_char.produced_by: WF4 'Approval Gate' code node AFTER F-02. fnv1aHex(s) = fnv1aPass(s, 0x811c9dc5) + fnv1aPass('K2|' + s + '|K2', 0x01000193) - two independent FNV-1a passes with different offset bases over differently salted input, 8 hex characters each, concatenated to 16. The n8n Code sandbox has no crypto module, which is why this is a doubled FNV rather than a real digest.
new_16_char.collision_probability: the same ~1% point moves beyond about 600 million deliveries

delivery_key_formats.normEmail: strips 'Name <addr>' to addr, trims, lowercases - so 'A. Smith <A.Smith@Example.COM>' and 'a.smith@example.com' are one delivery

expect.note: A non-zero old_8char_format_count is not automatically a failure - it is the known, accepted migration residue. It is a failure only when one of those rows belongs to an approval that is still PENDING (see wf4-pending-approval-not-stranded-on-legacy-key).

assertions: Every Communications.idempotency_key beginning with SND- matches ^SND-[0-9a-f]{16}(\|DRY)?$.
No SND- key is in the old format ^SND-[0-9a-f]{8}(\|DRY)?$, and none is in a third shape.
The dry-run key is exactly the send key with the literal suffix |DRY; the two must never be confused as separate deliveries.
communication_id for a real send is 'COM-' + the same hash; for a dry run it is 'COM-DRY-' + the same hash.
The key is a pure function of approval_id, action_id, draft_id, upper-cased channel and normalised recipient - no clock, no delivery_mode, no randomness.
Re-deriving the key from a row's own approval_id/action_id/draft_id/channel/recipient must reproduce that row's key; if it does not, the row is hand-edited or the key has collided.
target_unresolved_reason: kind is "invariant": not executed by harness/run.js.
